stance.label: Record point gain · flows not back · stick to the plan

headline: Taiex posts its biggest-ever point gain, up 8.99% back above 40,000, but foreigners sell for a 7th day
summary: Today was a news-driven bounce, not a turn in flows: foreign investors sold into the rally and added futures shorts. By the rules Taiwan is back above the bear-market line and rated a pullback again, but 2 risk lights stay on. Regular investing continues as planned; next, watch when foreign selling stops, Dell's results tonight and PCE tomorrow night.

overview.lead: Taiwan followed the Nvidia news to its biggest-ever point gain, but foreigners sold for a 7th day and added futures shorts: this is a sharp bounce, not a turn in flows.
points: The Taiex rose 8.99%; its intraday gain of 3,368 points was a record.
More than 500 listed and OTC stocks hit limit-up, including TSMC (2330), MediaTek (2454) and Hon Hai (2317).
The biggest gainer was last month's worst sector, electronic components: up 9.6% today, still down 32.8% over a month.
Asia rallied together: Korea's KOSPI rose 6.98% and Japan rose 4.15%.
By the rules Taiwan is back to a "pullback in an uptrend", but 2 risk lights stay on.

focus.lead: Among the nine tracked names, 0050 was strongest with a limit-up day; the three Taiwan-related funds' NAVs do not yet reflect today's rally.
points: 0050 rose 10.0% and is just 0.6% below its 200-day line.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) was −41.7% from its peak on the 11/23 NAV and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) −36.9%; today's tech rally is not in yet.
The two Taiwan tech funds share 6 of their top-ten names, about 27% by weight, so their next NAVs should rebound together.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV is still at 11/20, missing both days of Taiwan's rebound.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) NAV rose 7.8% on 11/23, already reflecting Nvidia (NVDA)'s surge.
SPY and QQQ get new prints tonight; AB American Growth (LU0683600562) NAV rose 4.0% on 11/23.

position.lead: By the framework, today's rally triggered nothing new and more than doubled 0050's distance to its fifth tier.
points: 0050 has used 70% of its reserve; the fifth tier is 14.8% away.
QQQ has used 45% of its reserve; the fourth tier is 6.7% away.
SPY has used 25% of its reserve; the third tier is 8.3% away.
AB American Growth has used 25% of its reserve; the third tier is 8.5% away.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan is 6.7% from its fifth tier (11/20 NAV); Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) is 10.5% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and AB International Technology have used all tiers.

macro.lead: Rates did not ease: markets still bet on a December hike, and a stronger dollar pushed the Taiwan dollar lower even on a huge up day.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.92% and the 2-year 4.63% (11/23).
New York Fed President Williams said inflation remains elevated; a 25 bp hike in December is fully priced.
The US Dollar Index rose to 104.53, a near 20-month high.
The Taiwan dollar reversed to 32.98 intraday; limit-up heavyweights meant foreigners could not buy even if they wanted to.
The high-yield spread is 3.76% (11/20), still well below the warning line.

sentiment.lead: One big day did not wash out the fear: the Fear & Greed index is still at extreme fear, and Taiwan's breadth stays near the lows.
points: CNN Fear & Greed is 17, still extreme fear.
VIX is 26.62, still above its long-run median of 17.6.
The 9-day VIX at 27.76 is above the 3-month at 25.5, so short-term hedging demand has not faded.
Only 15% of Taiwan stocks are above their 200-day line and 8% above their 50-day line.
Most analysts stay cautious, expecting Taiwan stocks to drift back to fundamentals in the short run.

sectors.lead: The hardest-hit tech names bounced most while old-economy and defensive sectors lagged: a classic oversold rebound.
points: Electronic components rose 9.6% and optoelectronics 8.4%, both the worst sectors over the past month.
Financials also rose nearly 9% intraday; almost every heavyweight hit limit-up.
Food rose only 3.3% and textiles 4.3%, as money moved back into tech.
Oil, power and gas fell 1.3%, the only major sector in the red.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan set a points record, but flows did not follow: foreigners sold for a 7th day and the three institutional groups sold NT$123.0B combined.
points: The Taiex rose 8.99% to close at 40,122, back above the bear-market line.
TSMC closed limit-up at NT$2,230, adding about 1,600 points intraday, nearly half the gain.
Foreign investors sold NT$50.4B, their 7th straight day of net selling.
Foreign net selling over 20 days is about NT$1.08 trillion, and a huge up day did not change the direction.
Dealers sold NT$81.0B while investment trusts bought NT$8.4B.
Foreign net short Taiex futures stand at 103,000 contracts, up about 5,300 contracts in five days.
Margin balances fell 31.6% in 20 days (11/23): deleveraging has gone deep.

watch.lead: Two things next: whether Taiwan holds the bear-market line, and whether Dell tonight and PCE tomorrow night let fundamentals take over from the news.
points: The Taiex bear-market line is 39,858; today closed 0.7% above it.
The first day foreigners turn net buyers is the first sign flows are stabilizing.
Dell (DELL) reports after the US close tonight, a test of AI server demand; US consumer confidence is also out.
On the evening of 11/25 US PCE inflation and Q3 GDP set December rate-hike expectations.
US markets close for Thanksgiving on 11/26 and close early on 11/27.
On 12/1 Huang sits for closed-door House interviews, the next hurdle for Nvidia's concerns.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan closed back above the bear-market line, so its rating moves from bear market back to "pullback in an uptrend, risk rising"; the US is still a pullback.
points: Trend: the Taiex is 3.5% below its 200-day line and has closed below it for 7 days, but the line is still rising.
Systemic risk lights: 2 are on, the US below its 200-day line and broken Taiwan breadth (only 15% above the 200-day line).
Credit, the economy and financial conditions are not in trouble yet; closest to turning on is the high-yield spread, up 0.49 points in a month against a 0.75 trigger.
Capitulation signals: two are on, margin down 31.6% in 20 days and a breadth washout.
History: since 2000, all 10 Taiwan declines that reached this level went past −20%, with a median low of −28.7%.
Only 4 were as fast as this one, too few to rely on; 2 of them went past −30%.
What would change the call: a close back below 39,858 means bear-market territory again.
5 closes below 41,597 with a flat 200-day line means weak.

news.title: The Taiex rose 3,310.46 points, or 8.99%, to 40,122.35 on turnover of NT$419.4B
news.read: The biggest point gain on record, closing back above the 39,858 bear-market line; by the rules Taiwan is a pullback again.

news.title: Record intraday gain of up to 3,368 points; TSMC limit-up at NT$2,230 adding about 1,600 points; more than 500 stocks limit-up
news.read: TSMC and tech heavyweights drove the rally; 0050 hit limit-up and the two Taiwan tech funds' next NAVs should rebound sharply.

news.title: Institutions net sold NT$123.0B: foreigners NT$50.4B, dealers NT$81.0B, investment trusts bought NT$8.4B
news.read: Institutions sold more on a huge up day and foreigners have sold for 7 straight days; the bounce lacks flow support.

news.title: TSMC, MediaTek, Hon Hai, Quanta, Wistron and other heavyweights all hit limit-up; semiconductor and electronic component stocks rose over 9%
news.read: Cathay Taiwan High Dividend's top two names, TSMC and MediaTek, both hit limit-up, so its next NAV should rebound strongly.

news.title: Asia rallied: the KOSPI rose 6.98% above 5,000 and the Nikkei 225 rose 4.15%; analysts warned of a return to fundamentals
news.read: Japan was led by tech names such as Advantest and Tokyo Electron; Fidelity Japan Value is mostly financials and benefits less.

news.title: The Taiwan dollar reversed to 32.98 intraday; the Dollar Index hit 104.53, a near 20-month high, with a December hike fully priced
news.read: Stocks surged but the currency did not, so foreign money did not flow in; a strong dollar and hike pressure still block a return.

news.title: FSC conditional short-sale curbs from 11/20: stocks closing down 3.5% or more cannot be shorted below the prior close next day; lending-sale cap cut to 1%
news.read: The curbs are still in place and limit shorting; their removal would be a sign the market is back to normal.

news.title: Short US week: Dell results on 11/24, PCE and Q3 GDP on 11/25, Thanksgiving holiday on 11/26
news.read: For the bounce to last, fundamentals must take over: Dell tests AI server demand and PCE sets December hike odds.
